solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thus America carrying burden becomes dozy

indicators.note: one piece carrying another holds it inside, so the word for thus is opened up to take the burden

parts.note: thus means so
to lumber someone is to burden them; lumber is an encumbrance

explanation.surface: A nation weighed down by its load grows sleepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts the burden inside the word for thus; 'becomes' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe someone drowsy and inclined to sleep.

clue.text: More than one bloodsucker strikes to secure victim

indicators.note: the strikes secure the victim by holding it inside

parts.note: to lam is to strike or thrash
prey is a victim

explanation.surface: Several leeches lash out to grab their prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: eel-like fish that attach to hosts and suck their blood.

clue.text: Order set up to imprison a Communist leader

indicators.note: the turned order holds the a inside, imprisoning it
set up in a down clue means written upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A command issued to jail a Communist leader.
explanation.walkthrough: OM read upwards is MO, which holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Chairman Mao Zedong led Communist China.

clue.text: Boy climbing tree with minimal energy

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
minimal energy is just its first letter

parts.note: the lime is a tree, the linden

explanation.surface: A lad shins up a tree with hardly any effort.
explanation.walkthrough: E then LIME, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a boy's name, as in Rousseau's educational novel about a boy.

clue.text: See sort that could turn out murderer in mythology

indicators.note: the letters could turn out differently, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a certain type of person may prove to be a mythical killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Greek myth he killed his mother Clytemnestra to avenge his father.

clue.text: Conservative in group, heretical and bigoted

indicators.note: the conservative letter goes in the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group
Arian describes the heresy of Arius, who denied Christ's full divinity

explanation.surface: A Tory within a faction, unorthodox and intolerant.
explanation.walkthrough: SET holds C, then ARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sectarian attitudes are narrow-minded and prejudiced against other groups.

clue.text: River that's more beautiful between banks?

indicators.note: what lies between the banks is the stretch without its two edge letters, the outer letters being the banks

parts.note: more beautiful means fairer

explanation.surface: Asks whether a river looks prettier when confined between its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIRER loses its outer letters F and R, leaving the river. The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a named English river flowing through Leeds.

clue.text: A star drinking nothing, overturning fizzy water

indicators.note: the star takes the reversed nothing inside it, drinking it in

parts.note: Polaris is the Pole Star

indicators.note: overturning in a down clue turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A celebrity on the wagon knocks over a glass of sparkling water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' reads the word for nothing upwards, giving LIN, which the star takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a brand of German sparkling mineral water.

clue.text: Dish of fish eggs: it's served up

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means put upwards, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: A plate of caviar is brought to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: ROE then ITS read upwards, STI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Swiss dish of fried grated potato.

clue.text: A special moment in which one's collected fossil

indicators.note: the shuffled letters have one collected inside them, holding it within
special here means specially arranged, signalling the letters of moment are rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A moment of discovery when a fossil hunter picks up a find.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then MOMENT rearranged as MMONTE with I (one) collected inside to make MMONITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a spiral-shelled extinct mollusc, one of the commonest fossils.

clue.text: Block Yankee, creating stir

parts.note: to block a pipe is to choke it
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Blocking an American player causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is not commotion but British slang for prison, as is chokey.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: both are informal British words for a prison or jail.

clue.text: River, Charlie? You and I will catch that fish

indicators.note: the pronoun pair will catch the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: you and I together are we
a charlie is British slang for a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Addressing Charlie by a river: the two of us will land that fish.
explanation.walkthrough: WE holds R and ASS. A charlie is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a brightly coloured marine fish of the family Labridae.

clue.text: Seriously performing only, I warble about heartless fellow

parts.note: sole means only

indicators.note: heartless means losing the middle letter of the word for fellow

parts.note: a man is a fellow
to warble is to sing

explanation.surface: Someone sings only about a cold-hearted man.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLE, then MN (MAN without its heart), then I SING; 'about' only says what the singing concerns.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to solemnise a wedding is to perform it formally with ceremony.

clue.text: Group entering train to get drier

indicators.note: the group goes into the word for train, entering it

parts.note: to train is to teach
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A party of passengers boarding a train to dry off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway train but is the verb, teach; 'drier' is a thing that dries.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a cloth used to dry dishes is something that dries.

clue.text: European seriously drunk in bar

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit in the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A European is very drunk in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb, BAN, holding YELORUSSI, the anagram of SERIOUSLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a native of Belarus, an Eastern European country, under its older name.

clue.text: Hospital in Somerset redone as accommodation for the elderly

indicators.note: the hospital letter goes in the rearranged county
redone suggests the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital in the English county of Somerset is converted into housing for old people.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is rearranged to RESTOMES with H placed in it. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: residential homes where elderly people live with care.

clue.text: Famous Argentinian tucked into cooked pie and sausage

indicators.note: the Argentinian is tucked into the rearranged letters
cooked suggests the letters are messed about

parts.note: Juan or Eva Perón, famous Argentine figures

explanation.surface: A celebrated Argentine eats a baked pie and a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE rearranged as PEI holds PERON.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a spicy Italian-style salami used on pizzas.

clue.text: Female home full of love attended by stars who bring good news?

parts.note: miss is a girl or unmarried woman

indicators.note: the word for home is full of the love letter, holding it inside

parts.note: in means at home
love is O, a zero score in tennis
Aries is a constellation of stars, the Ram

explanation.surface: A woman at home, in love, consults her horoscope for good news.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS, then IN holding O to make ION, then ARIES. The question mark flags that the good news is the Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: evangelists spread the Gospel, whose name means good news.

clue.text: Coming soon as a sale item?

definitions.meaning: something coming soon is awaiting you, lying ahead
goods for sale are kept in a shop's stock

explanation.surface: Asks whether a product is about to go on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: an idiom for what awaits, and the literal place shop goods are held.

clue.text: Umpire, old, with room for improvement

parts.note: a ref, referee, is an umpire

explanation.surface: An elderly umpire says there is space to do better.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reform is change for the better.

clue.text: Haggard female beset by fairies passes away

indicators.note: the female is beset by the fairies, surrounded by them

parts.note: peris are fairies in Persian myth
She is the title character of H. Rider Haggard's novel

explanation.surface: A worn-out woman surrounded by fairies dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like worn out but points to the novelist H. Rider Haggard, whose 'She' supplies SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to perish is to die, a euphemism being to pass away.

clue.text: Naval officer's clique drink

parts.note: PO is a Petty Officer, and the apostrophe s adds S
a set is a clique or circle

explanation.surface: The petty officer's circle has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hot milk drink curdled with ale or wine.

clue.text: Small cat or dog, the one giving chase

parts.note: a cat or a dog is a pet
in the game of tag the chaser is called it

explanation.surface: A little animal is the one doing the chasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: French for little, used in English for small or minor.

clue.text: An element of singular dislike

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
odium is hatred or strong dislike

explanation.surface: One element of a peculiar aversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' looks like odd but is the grammar abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soft metallic chemical element, symbol Na.

clue.text: Not terribly keen about final decision-maker? Precisely!

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word not is badly mangled into a new order
the word for keen goes about the editor, surrounding him

parts.note: hot means keen or eager
the editor, ED, has the final say on what is printed

explanation.surface: Someone unenthusiastic about the person who makes the last call answers exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns NOT into ONT. The editor is the final decision-maker because what goes into print is his or her call.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: arriving on the dot means arriving at exactly the right time.

clue.text: Bird in science unit

definitions.meaning: the electromagnetic unit of physics, abbreviated as these three letters

explanation.surface: A bird kept in a university science department.
explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: a flightless Australian bird, and the abbreviation for electromagnetic unit.

clue.text: Gladstone's epithet's recalled in a haze

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Gladstone was nicknamed the GOM, Grand Old Man, and the apostrophe s adds S

explanation.surface: The Victorian statesman's nickname is remembered only vaguely.
explanation.walkthrough: W. E. Gladstone, the Victorian British Prime Minister, was called the Grand Old Man, GOM; GOMS turned back gives the haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: smog is a polluted haze of smoke and fog.

clue.text: Provider of printed notes for performers

definitions.text: Provider of printed notes for performers

parts.words: Provider of printed notes for performers
parts.note: printed notes sound like a handout or banknotes, but they are musical notes on paper for players

explanation.surface: Sounds like someone handing out programme notes or cash to actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: printed scores give musicians the notes to play.
